description: The $-variables that describe the running system (version, platform, hardware, directories, user and licence), configure the session (paths, packages, contexts, numeric limits, language, encodings, internet access, unit system) and report the evaluation environment (cloud vs. local, links, geolocation, devices), plus SystemInformation.

tools.name: $Version
tools.description: String describing the Wolfram Language version, platform and build date (e.g. "14.2.0 for Microsoft Windows (64-bit) (December 26, 2024)"); $VersionNumber is the numeric major.minor version (14.2), $ReleaseNumber the release within it and $CreationDate the build date. Use $VersionNumber in code that must branch on version.

tools.name: $SystemID
tools.description: Short string identifying the platform and architecture ("Windows-x86-64", "MacOSX-ARM64", "Linux-x86-64"), used to locate LibraryLink binaries in paclets; $OperatingSystem gives "Windows", "MacOSX" or "Unix", $System the full platform name, $MachineType the machine class and $SystemWordLength the word size (64). Branch on these for platform-specific paths and executables.

tools.name: $ProcessorCount
tools.description: Number of processor cores available to the kernel (the default number of parallel subkernels launched by LaunchKernels); $ProcessorType names the CPU architecture ("x86-64", "ARM64") and $ByteOrdering gives the endianness (1 big, -1 little) relevant for BinaryRead/BinaryWrite. $ConfiguredKernels lists the configured parallel kernel setup.
tools.example:
BinaryReadList["data.bin", "Real32", ByteOrdering -> $ByteOrdering]
ParallelTable[f[i], {i, 100}] (* uses up to $ProcessorCount kernels *)

tools.name: $MachineName
tools.description: Host name of the computer; $MachineID is a hardware-derived identifier used for licensing, $MachineAddresses lists the IP addresses of the network interfaces, $NetworkInterfaces their names, $MachineDomains the network domains and $NetworkConnected whether the machine has network access. Use them in logs and to select machine-specific configuration.
tools.example:
config = Switch[$MachineName, "hpc-node1", hpcSettings, _, defaultSettings]
Print["run on ", $MachineName, " at ", DateString[]]

tools.name: $Username
tools.description: Login name of the operating-system user running the kernel; $ProcessID is the kernel's OS process id, $ParentProcessID that of its parent (front end or shell), $SystemShell the default shell used by Run, and $SessionID a unique identifier of the kernel session. Handy for temporary-file naming and diagnostics.

tools.name: $BaseDirectory
tools.description: Directory of system-wide Wolfram configuration and installed packages/paclets shared by all users; $UserBaseDirectory is the per-user equivalent (containing Applications, Kernel/init.m, Paclets, SystemFiles), $InstallationDirectory the product installation root and $InitialDirectory the working directory at start-up. Packages placed in $UserBaseDirectory/Applications are found by Needs automatically.

tools.name: $TemporaryDirectory
tools.description: Directory for temporary files (CreateFile[] and CreateTemporary[] put files there); $HomeDirectory is the user's home (listed elsewhere), $RootDirectory the file-system root and $CacheBaseDirectory the location of downloaded/cached data (documentation, entity data, NetModel weights). Clean $CacheBaseDirectory to reclaim disk space.
tools.example:
f = CreateTemporary[]; Export[f, data, "CSV"]; ... DeleteFile[f]
FileByteCount /@ FileNames["*", $CacheBaseDirectory, Infinity] // Total

tools.name: $Path
tools.description: List of directories searched by Get, Needs and FindFile for package files (in order); append project directories to make your packages loadable by context name. $Packages lists the contexts of packages loaded so far and $Context is the current context for symbol creation ($ContextPath is listed elsewhere).

tools.name: $Input
tools.description: Name of the file currently being read by Get (empty string interactively), useful for locating resources relative to a package file together with $InputFileName (listed); $Output is the list of output streams for Print (add a file stream to tee output), $Messages the streams for messages, $Echo streams echoing input, and $Urgent streams for urgent messages. Redirecting $Output is the classic way to log a script.

tools.name: $Epilog
tools.description: Symbol whose value is evaluated when the kernel exits (the end.m hook), used to close files, flush logs or delete temporary objects on Quit/Exit; the start-up counterparts are the init.m files in $BaseDirectory/Kernel and $UserBaseDirectory/Kernel (and InitializationValue for simple settings).

tools.name: $MaxMachineNumber
tools.description: Largest positive machine-precision real (about 1.798*10^308); $MinMachineNumber the smallest positive normalized one, $MachineEpsilon the spacing of machine numbers near 1 (2.22*10^-16), and $MaxNumber / $MinNumber the largest/smallest arbitrary-precision numbers the kernel can represent. Use them for overflow checks and tolerance choices in numerical code.

tools.name: $MaxPrecision
tools.description: Maximum precision (in digits) allowed for arbitrary-precision numbers, Infinity by default; $MinPrecision is the minimum precision (0 by default) below which results are not allowed to drop. Setting $MinPrecision = $MaxPrecision = n forces fixed-precision arithmetic, useful to emulate hardware behaviour or stop precision loss in iterative algorithms.
tools.example: Block[{$MinPrecision = 30, $MaxPrecision = 30}, Nest[Sqrt[# + 1] &, N[1, 30], 100]] (* precision stays at 30 *)

tools.name: $Language
tools.description: Default language for messages and text functions ("English" by default); TextString, IntegerName, DateString names and WordTranslation defaults depend on it. InitializationValue[$Language] = "..." persists the choice across sessions.

tools.name: $ImportFormats
tools.description: List of all file/data formats Import understands on this installation, and $ExportFormats those Export can write; $CharacterEncodings lists supported character encodings and $FontFamilies the fonts available to the front end. Use them to validate format names before batch conversions.

tools.name: $AllowInternet
tools.description: Global switch (True/False) for whether the kernel may access the internet: when False, entity data, paclet downloads, URLRead, WolframAlpha and similar functions fail immediately instead of connecting. Set it False for air-gapped or reproducible offline runs; $NetworkConnected reports actual connectivity.
tools.example:
$AllowInternet = False;
CountryData["France", "Population"] (* fails offline unless cached *)

tools.name: $UnitSystem
tools.description: Default unit system ("Metric" or "Imperial") used when functions such as UnitConvert[q, "SI"]... choose target units, CityData/WeatherData return quantities, and TargetUnits -> Automatic is applied; initially derived from the OS locale. Set it explicitly in scripts so output units do not depend on the machine.

tools.name: $GeoLocation
tools.description: The current geographic position of the machine (GeoPosition, determined from IP/OS location services or set manually), used as the default for Here, GeoGraphics centering, Sunrise/Sunset, WeatherData and LocalTime; $GeoLocationCountry, $GeoLocationCity and $GeoLocationSource give the derived country/city and how the location was obtained. Set $GeoLocation explicitly for reproducible scripts.

tools.name: $LicenseID
tools.description: Licence identification string of the running kernel; $LicenseExpirationDate gives the expiry date, $LicenseServer the licence server for network licences and $MaxLicenseProcesses / $MaxLicenseSubprocesses the process limits that bound LaunchKernels. Useful in support diagnostics and to guard parallel start-up.

tools.name: $EvaluationEnvironment
tools.description: String naming the context in which the kernel is evaluating: "Session" (interactive notebook/terminal), "Script" (wolframscript -script/-file), "Subkernel" (parallel subkernel), "CloudObject"/"WebAPI"/"WebForm"/"ScheduledTask" (cloud deployments) and others; $CloudEvaluation is True inside the cloud. Branch on it to disable dialogs and interactivity in scripts and deployed code.
tools.example: report[x_] := Switch[$EvaluationEnvironment, "Session", PrintTemporary[x], "Script", WriteString["stderr", x <> "\n"], _, Null]

tools.name: $ParentLink
tools.description: The LinkObject through which the kernel talks to its parent (front end or controlling program), Null for a stand-alone kernel; $Linked is True when a link exists, $CurrentLink is the link currently being serviced in an installed external program and $CommandLine (listed) shows how the kernel was started. Test $ParentLink === Null to detect a headless, script-driven kernel.
tools.example:
headless = $ParentLink === Null || $FrontEnd === Null;
If[headless, UsingFrontEnd[Export["p.png", plot]], Export["p.png", plot]]

tools.name: $TimeUnit
tools.description: Minimum time interval (in seconds) resolvable by TimeUsed/Timing on the platform (e.g. 1/1000); $ModuleNumber is the counter appended to Module local variable names (x$123), incremented for every Module/Unique call, and $Line the current input line number. Mostly of interest for benchmarking and debugging generated symbols.
tools.example:
Module[{x}, x] (* x$nnn where nnn = $ModuleNumber - 1 *)
Timing[expr] (* resolution limited by $TimeUnit *)

tools.name: $ImagingDevices
tools.description: List of cameras available to CurrentImage/ImageCapture, with $DefaultImagingDevice the one used by default; $AudioInputDevices / $AudioOutputDevices list microphones and speakers used by AudioCapture and AudioStream, with $DefaultAudioInputDevice / $DefaultAudioOutputDevice the defaults. Use them to select hardware in lab-automation scripts.

tools.name: $Notebooks
tools.description: True when the kernel is connected to a notebook front end (so Dynamic, Manipulate, dialogs and typeset output work) and False in terminal or script sessions; the standard test for choosing between interactive and text-only behaviour. $FrontEnd (listed) gives the front-end object itself.

tools.name: $RandomGeneratorState
tools.description: Opaque object capturing the complete state of the random number generator; save it and restore it with $RandomGeneratorState = state (or use BlockRandom) to reproduce a random sequence exactly, more precisely than SeedRandom when the generator has already been used. RandomGeneratorState objects are also what BlockRandom localizes.
tools.usage:
state = $RandomGeneratorState
$RandomGeneratorState = state
BlockRandom[expr]
SeedRandom[n]
SeedRandom[n, Method -> "MersenneTwister"]

tools.name: $SystemCharacterEncoding
tools.description: Default character encoding of the operating system (e.g. "WindowsANSI" on Windows, "UTF-8" on macOS/Linux), used for file names, RunProcess I/O and Environment values; $CharacterEncoding (listed) is the encoding for text streams and defaults to UTF-8 in recent versions. Convert explicitly when RunProcess output contains non-ASCII text on Windows.

tools.name: $EmbedCodeEnvironments
tools.description: List of target environments supported by EmbedCode (e.g. "Python", "Java", "JavaScript", "C#", "Swift", "HTML", "R") for generating client code that calls a deployed cloud API; EmbedCode[obj, env] produces an EmbeddingObject with the source code. Check it before generating client libraries.

tools.name: SystemInformation
tools.description: Returns a structured report (or association with "Kernel", "FrontEnd", "Devices", "Links", "Parallel", "Network" sections) of the system configuration: versions, directories, licence, memory, processor, installed paclets, network settings. SystemInformation["Kernel", "prop"] fetches one value; "Small" gives a brief summary. Use it in bug reports and environment checks.

tools.name: $SystemTimeZone
tools.description: Time zone of the operating system as a numeric UTC offset or IANA name; $TimeZone (listed) is the zone the kernel uses for dates and defaults to it, and $TimeZoneEntity the corresponding TimeZone entity. Set $TimeZone = "UTC" (or 0) in servers and scripts to make date output machine-independent.

tools.name: $PersistenceBase
tools.description: Root of the local persistence store used by PersistentSymbol/PersistentObject and InitializationValue, with $PersistencePath the ordered list of PersistenceLocation objects searched ("KernelSession", "FrontEndSession", "Local", "Cloud", ...); $LocalBase is the root for LocalObject files and $LocalSymbolBase for LocalSymbol values. Inspect them to find where persisted values live on disk.

tools.name: $Permissions
tools.description: Default permissions applied by CloudDeploy, CloudPut and related functions when no Permissions option is given ("Private" by default); set it to "Public" in a session that deploys many public objects. $EvaluationCloudObject, $RequesterAddress and $RequesterWolframID (cloud-side context variables) are listed with $CloudBase.

tools.name: $DisplayFunction
tools.description: Legacy global function applied to graphics output for display (Identity by default in modern versions); DisplayFunction -> Identity was the pre-Version-6 way to suppress plot display and still appears in old code, where it can simply be removed. Modern code controls display with semicolons and Show.
tools.example:
(* old code *) p = Plot[Sin[x], {x, 0, 6}, DisplayFunction -> Identity]; Show[p, DisplayFunction -> $DisplayFunction]
(* modern *) p = Plot[Sin[x], {x, 0, 6}]; p
